To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
habit learning interferes in a context-specific fashion with goal-direction, and this is consistent with the idea that habit is context-specific, whereas goal-direction is context-general.

(1) Habit learning interferes with the goal direction of an instrumental action in a manner similar to other types of retroaction interference; (2) Habit learning does not destroy action learning, but rather interferes with it; (3) Habit and goal direction are dissociable in that the goal direction of a response remains intact in one context after habit learning in a different context.

(1) habit learning does not destroy action memory, but (2) habit learning does retroactively interfere with goal direction in the context in which the habit is learned, and (3) this context-dependent interference is specific to goal direction and does not occur in the context of habit performance.
